name: Community First
description: Speaks to the regulars before the newcomers. Opens by answering the last episode's comments, puts a question to the audience early, and only then gets to what this episode is. The links and support block is a real section rather than a footer.
architecture: Greets returning viewers, asks a question, then the episode, then links.

sections.instruction: Two or three sentences addressed to viewers who have watched before, connecting this episode to the running thread of the channel. Do not recap a specific previous episode by name unless the story context names one.
One question to the audience that this episode gives them something to say about. It must be answerable in a comment in one line, and must not be a yes or no question.
Describe this episode: what it covers, why it is worth the time. Write it as though continuing a conversation already in progress rather than introducing yourself.
Leave this section empty. The channel's own links, playlists and support destinations are inserted from the publishing profile, so write nothing here.
One sentence thanking the people who watch to the end. No request attached to it.
Emit only hashtags, on a single line, separated by spaces. No sentence, no heading, no commentary.

title_plan.guidance: Written as though to someone who already subscribes. May reference the series or the running thread. Avoid explaining the premise of the channel in the title.

tag_plan.guidance: for this community-facing episode, mixing the channel's own recurring terms with the episode subject

constraints: Address returning viewers before explaining anything to newcomers.
Ask exactly one question of the audience, and make it answerable in one line.
Never stack multiple calls to action in the same paragraph.
